summary: World Cup Hub system synthesis and token emission completed from the accepted fixture-led concept, checksum-current Semantic OS Markdown policy, and 19 authored component contracts. Strict component validation now reports 19 authored contracts, 28 primitive reconciliation records, three approved waivers, and no unresolved component token references; all 127 authored token references resolve through current --ds-* variables and complete light/dark semantic role sets. The existing visual-asset-manifest/v2 remains integrated and provenance-valid. One downstream visual prompt defect remains: the preserved hero-image prompt still describes a first-viewport landing hero and the planned card-thumbnail remains generic, which conflicts with the accepted fixture-led avoid_layouts. Fixing that safely requires changing the prompt-slot inference/generation contract and migrating the reviewed integrated asset provenance, so no generated prompt or manifest was hand-edited in this compiler stage.
decisions: Compile only from the accepted fixture-led command desk concept and retain its synchronized match rail, first-screen contract, and explicit rejection of generic hero/card-grid layouts.
Treat the checksum-current runtime policy embedded in docs/color-reference.md as the only application semantic color authority; keep the approved identity-only raw-color exception separate.

Accept the generated component system only when all 19 token maps retain token_provenance=authored-input, all 28 primitive reconciliation decisions and three approved waivers survive, and every authored token reference resolves to a current --ds-* variable.

Preserve the visual-asset-manifest/v2 integrated Codex asset, generation run, candidate, original file, prompt packet and slot hashes, and runtime integration evidence without hand-editing provenance.

Do not rewrite the prompt packet merely to rename generic slots: changing packet or slot content would invalidate the reviewed integrated asset's exact prompt hashes unless the prompt generator and provenance migration are updated together.
Record the generic hero/card-thumbnail prompt conflict as a failed product-alignment gate rather than incorrectly reporting the visual prompt stage ready.
